findings.title: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff access to Authorise endpoint
findings.claim: CardsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, while Authorise is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)]. In ASP.NET Core, controller- and action-level authorization attributes are evaluated conjunctively (logical AND), so Authorise requires both Customer and Staff policies. Staff or card-network callers lacking the Customer policy will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CardsController class and place [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] individually on Issue, Freeze, Unfreeze, and Cancel.
findings.requirement_link: Card payment authorisation (POST api/cards/{id}/authorise, Staff policy): Calls ICardService.AuthoriseAsync(cardId, amount, merchant) with no customer ownership check.

findings.title: Class-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff from payment authorisation
findings.claim: CardsController is decorated with `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` at class level. In ASP.NET Core, action-level Authorize attributes are additive to class-level attributes, requiring callers of `Authorise` to satisfy both Customer and Staff policies simultaneously. Staff callers and card-network callers without Customer credentials will be denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
findings.evidence:

findings.suggested_fix: Remove `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` from the controller class declaration and apply it explicitly to `Issue`, `Freeze`, `Unfreeze`, and `Cancel`, leaving `Authorise` restricted only to `Policies.Staff`.
findings.requirement_link: Card payment authorisation (POST api/cards/{id}/authorise, Staff policy): Calls ICardService.AuthoriseAsync(cardId, amount, merchant) with no customer ownership check.

findings.title: Ad-hoc static in-memory account locking introduces memory leak and ineffective concurrency control
findings.claim: CardService introduces a static unbounded ConcurrentDictionary to lock account IDs during payment authorisation. This leaks SemaphoreSlim instances permanently in memory across the process lifecycle and provides no synchronization across multi-instance deployments; ledger operations should rely on database and ledger transactional guarantees.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> AccountLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Remove AccountLocks and rely on ILedger.PostTransferAsync and database transactional/concurrency mechanisms to handle transfer concurrency.
findings.requirement_link: Authorisation approval rules: When the card is Active, rounded amount is within 2000m, and the account has sufficient funds, funds move strictly via ILedger.PostTransferAsync from card.AccountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, account.Currency) for the rounded amount.

findings.title: Static AccountLocks dictionary grows indefinitely, leaking SemaphoreSlim instances
findings.claim: AccountLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim instance for every account processed by AuthoriseAsync in a static ConcurrentDictionary without eviction or cleanup. In a long-running service processing authorisations across many customer accounts, this dictionary grows monotonically and permanently retains SemaphoreSlim objects in memory.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> AccountLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Remove in-memory static semaphore locks in favor of database/ledger concurrency controls, or utilize a bounded/evicting lock manager to prevent unbounded memory growth.

findings.title: Debit card numbers generated using cryptographically weak PRNG
findings.claim: Card numbers are sensitive financial identifiers generated using `Random.Shared`. Because `Random.Shared` is a non-cryptographic PRNG, an attacker observing generated card numbers could determine internal PRNG state and predict card numbers issued to other users.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt64(0, 1_000_000_000_000_000L)` instead of `Random.Shared` to generate unpredictable card numbers.
findings.requirement_link: Creates an Active Card with a generated 16-digit Number annotated with [Pii]

findings.claim: The test asserts ThrowsAnyAsync<Exception> instead of the specific ArgumentOutOfRangeException thrown by CardService. AuthoriseAsync. This allows any unintended failure (such as NullReferenceException or KeyNotFoundException) to pass unnoticed.
